title.narrative: Girls Empowerment and Learning for All Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) Angola - Girls Empowerment and Learning for All Project is to empower Angolan youth, especially girls, and to improve learning quality for all. The project has the following three components: The first component seeks to empower Angolan girls, with certain activities also targeting boys. The component aims to (a) provide adolescent health services, (b) expand opportunities for second chance education and life skills, and (c) keep girls in school through demand-side actions. The second component addresses those challenges pertaining more directly to the education system, building on the experiences of the ongoing PAT (P122700). This component is organized around sub-components that relate to (a) expanding education infrastructure, (b) improving the quality of teaching and learning, and (c) minimizing COVID-19 disruptions. Component 3 is the Project management, monitoring, and evaluation.
To empower Angolan youth, especially girls, and to improve learning quality for all.

title.narrative: Proportion of girls as percentage of total students enrolled in cycle 1 in Project municipalities

comment.narrative:
Gender parity in cycle 1 of secondary, calculated as percentage of students that are girls. Achieving 50 percent girls' enrollment would represent gender parity. Achieving 46 percent means cutting the gender gap in half.
This indicator has improved during the past semester from 42% to 48.8% and is expected to continue progressing. This indicator will be revised in the planned restructuring. The baseline will be revised to 48.2, in line with data reported in the 2021/22 statistical yearbook. (The 2020/2021 Statistical yearbook = 48.5% and 2021/2022 Statistical yearbook = 48.2%). The end target will be revised as an increase to 49% is expected with the continued implementation of the scholarship program.

title.narrative: Number of students completing second chance education with integrated life skills (Disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative:
Number of students having approved modules 1, 2, and 3 of second chance education program (EJA) in primary, and cycles 1 and 2 of EJA in secondary. Targets have been calculated based on program expansion, assuming the program maintains the quality of delivery as reflected in the pass rate (highest pass rate of the three modules taken - 77%).
This indicator has increased from 20,119 to 62,782 over the past semester. However, the end target will be revised in the planned restructuring of the project. Proposed changes include adjusting the baseline to zero resulting in a reduction of the indicator from previous ISR. The data sources and methodology will also be updated. These changes are motivated by the fact that the EMIS does not report data on the completion of EJA. The data will be sourced via KoboCollect by the municipal supervisors.

Girls benefitting from hygiene menstruation management program

comment.narrative:
Girls attending schools that have benefited from MHM activities, as delivered by NGOs or directly by schools. Activities to begin being reported on in 2023 (October). Indicator reflects number of girls receiving MHM kits and training.

Additionally, the definition of the indicator will be revised to: (Girls attending school who benefited from MHM activities carried out by NGOs, and benefited from the Menstrual Hygiene Kit).

title.narrative: Percent improvement in reading scores for 4th grade

comment.narrative:
Improvement in percentage points above previous reading score results, as measured through the application of national exams. For example, if 20 percent of students in grade 4 are deemed having achieved a functional level of literacy in the application of the 2023 national exam, by the end of the project, the target percentage for functionally literate students in grade 4 should be at least 24 percent. Baseline results for 2023 expected to be reported on by end of 2023.
This indicator definition will be revised during the planned restructuring to â€œStudents' reading level at the beginning of 4th Grade, measured through a zero score in the Reading comprehension subtask. Currently at 66%" for the 2022 EGRA. If 66% have a zero score, then 34% have some reading scoreâ€. Respectively the baseline (34%) and end target (34% + 4 = 34%) will be revised in function of the updated definition. The data source will be EGRA which is scheduled to take place prior to current project closure date.

The project will focus on construction of schools in contrast to rehabilitation of classrooms. Therefore, during the restructuring end target will be revised in line with the current expectations related to construction and rehabilitation works.

title.narrative: Application and publication of results from national/regional exams in Portuguese and Math

comment.narrative:
Number of large scale national or regional/international exams and assessments applied in Angola, for subjects covering (at least) Portuguese and math. These can be national exams developed just for Angola, regional exams (such as those instituted by SACMEQ), or international exams, such as PISA for development, or TIMSS. National level results must be published within 1 year of exam application in order for the indicator to be considered met.
This indicator definition will be revised during the planned restructuring to â€œNumber of large-scale national or regional/international assessments applied in Angola, for subjects that cover (at least) Portuguese and mathematics. These can be national assessments developed just for Angola, regional assessments (such as those established by SACMEQ) or international assessments such as PISA for development or TIMSS. The results at the national level must be published within 1 year after the assessments are applied for the indicator to be considered satisfiedâ€.

title.narrative: Proportion of teachers performing at or above satisfactory level

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures teacher performance, as estimated using the TEACH classroom observation instrument. The number is the proportion of teachers receiving a score of either 'satisfactory' or 'highly satisfactory', according to the instrument.
This indicator will be revised during the planned restructuring to adjust the baseline and end target in line with current project context (TEACH report 2022) and expected results.

title.narrative: Completion rate in cycle I of secondary education (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative:
As per UNESCO's Institute of Statistics, the completion rate is the percentage of a cohort of children or young people aged 3-5 years above the intended age for the last grade of each level of education who have completed that grade. The intended age for the last grade of each level of education is the age at which pupils would enter the grade if they had started school at the official primar entrance age, had studied full-time and had progressed without repeating or skipping a grade. In this case, the official age of entry into cycle 1 is 12 years, and the cycle has 3 grades, such that the intended age for the last grade is 14 years. In this case, 17-19 years (14 + 3 = 17 and 14 + 5 = 19) would be the reference age group for calculation of the cycle 1 of secondary completion rate.
The indicator definition will be revised during the planned restructuring to â€œCalculated by GEPE based on the ratio between the number of students enrolled for the first time in the 9th class (class completing the 1st cycle), regardless of their age, and the population aged 14 (theoretical age for completing the 1st cycle)â€. The baseline will also revised using the average of 2020 and 2021 observations, taken from the statistical yearbook. Observations from 2019 are disregarded as they were overestimated.

title.narrative: Students attending module 1, 2, 3 and cycle 1 of EJA

comment.narrative:
This indicator has made significant progress over the past semester reaching 372,571 students attending modules 1, 2 and 3 of the EJA program.
Total number of students registered for EJA, including students attending through schools, and through partners. Updated number reflects baseline value plus 17,310 students attending EJA classes as part of the Project implementation. 11,030 are female students, 6,154 are male; 17,184 are attending module 1, 2, and 3, and 126 are attending cycle 1.
The indicator baseline, end target, data source and methodology will be revised during the planned restructuring to align with current project context. Supervisors of the second chance education program will be responsible for data collection via KoboCollect during the process of monitoring and verification of classes. The proposed baseline will be zero which explains the reduction of this indicator from previous ISR.

title.narrative: Mechanism for PBF in the education sector developed and endorsed

comment.narrative:
A model for using performance-based financing in the education sector through provinces and/or municipalities, similar to that developed under the health sector, has been developed and endorsed by MED.
Following discussions with the Government, it was agreed that this indicator should be discontinued during the planned restructuring as this activity requires policy changes in terms of how schools are managed (transparency related to the flow of funds). Furthermore, the project does not support any activities that depend on a PBF mechanism.

title.narrative: Percentage of grievances addressed by the GM within six months

comment.narrative:
This indicators tracks the percentage of all grievances that have been received through the Project's Grievance Mechanism, that have been addressed by the PIU, the MED, or MINSA, depending on which is the competent authority for the cases lodged.
Over the past semester all grievances received were addressed.
The indicator definition will be revised during the planned restructuring by removing the word MoH from the definition. The proposed definition is â€œThis indicator tracks the percentage of all complaints that were received through the Project GRM and were forwarded for resolution by the PIU or MED depending on which is the competent authority for the cases presentedâ€.
